rows.text: Warsaw, 4 November 2026
Information from the meeting of the Monetary Policy Council held on 3-4 November 2026
The Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged: ▪ reference rate at 3.75%; ▪ lombard rate at 4.25%; ▪ deposit rate at 3.25%; ▪ rediscount rate at 3.80%; ▪ discount rate at 3.85%.
In 2026 Q3, annual GDP growth in the euro area and in the United States was close to their long-term averages.
At the same time, due to high energy commodity prices, global inflation has been elevated.
The outlook for global activity and inflation is subject to uncertainty, stemming, in particular, from the conflict in the Middle East.
In Poland, available data suggest that in 2026 Q3 annual GDP growth slowed down.
In September 2026 retail sales and industrial output increased in annual terms, while construction and assembly production fell.
Wage growth in the enterprise sector in 2026 Q3 was running close to the level observed in the first half of 2026.
At the same time, employment in this sector, continued to decrease in annual terms.
According to the Statistics Poland flash estimate, in October 2026 CPI inflation declined to 3.5% y/y (from 4.1% in September), mainly due to lower fuel prices compared to September.
Considering the Statistics Poland preliminary data, it can be estimated that inflation net of food and energy prices also decreased in October.
The Council became acquainted with the results of the November projection of inflation and GDP based on the NECMOD model.

In line with the projection, prepared under the assumption of unchanged NBP interest rates and taking into account data available until 15 October 2026, there is a 50-percent probability that the annual price growth will be in the range of 3.1 – 3.2% in 2026 (against 2.4 – 3.3% in the July 2026 projection), 3.1 – 5.3% in 2027 (compared to 1.5 – 4.0%) and 1.4 – 4.4% in 2028 (compared to 0.8 – 3.9%).

At the same time, the annual GDP growth – according to the projection – will be with a 50-percent probability in the range of 3.2 – 4.1% in 2026 (against 3.0 – 4.4% in the July 2026 projection), 1.9 – 3.8% in 2027 (compared to 1.8 – 3.7%) and 1.7 – 3.9% in 2028 (compared to 1.9 – 4.1%).
Against this background the Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged.
Further decisions of the Council will depend on incoming information regarding prospects for inflation and economic activity in Poland.
Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context.

The shape of fiscal policy, regulatory decisions regarding energy prices, changes in activity growth of the Polish economy and further developments in wage growth also remain risk factors for inflation outlook.

NBP will continue to take all necessary actions in order to ensure macroeconomic and financial stability, including above all to ensure inflation at the level consistent with the NBP inflation target in the medium term.
NBP may intervene in the foreign exchange market.
